# 1. Executive summary (non-technical)

**Model:** METIMMOX-1 — partitioned survival model (PSM) model at `c:/Users/benjampg/git/METIMMOX-1/model`
(commit `e098658`, model/ is an untracked subdirectory of the parent repo).

**Requested modules:** Module 1 (Transparency) and Module 3 (Verification). Modules 2 (Face validity), 4 (Cross-validation), and 5 (External validation) were not requested.

**Overall verdict: Fail**

The model is internally **not verified**: its core partitioned-survival partition is built from overall-survival (OS) and progression-free-survival (PFS) curves that are fit as two independent parametric models with no ordering constraint, and for the two biomarker-positive economic subgroups (CRP+, TMB/BRAF+) the fitted PFS curve exceeds the OS curve across roughly half of the 10-year extrapolated horizon. A silent `pmin(pfs, os)` clamp, surfaced only as an easily-missed `warning()`, forces the "progressed" health state to zero occupancy for that entire span — distorting the quality-adjusted life-year (QALY) and cost partition between progression-free and progressed care for exactly the arms the economic strategies are built to evaluate. Separately, the supporting documentation is internally inconsistent: a June 2026 single-model/no-TLR refactor was applied to the code and to `AGENTS.md` and the currently-rendered reports, but never propagated to the sibling `docs/README.md` or the in-repo manuscript, which still describe a three-biomarker, Model-A/B/C structure that no longer exists in code; and the documented default utility source (IPD-derived) contradicts the code's actual default (CORRECT trial), blocking reproduction of the manuscript's headline QALYs/ICERs from a fresh clone with default settings. Both defects were confirmed by independent evidence streams (black-box behavioural testing plus white-box code inspection for the curve-crossing issue; two independent documentation reviewers for the contradictions) and neither is disclosed as a known limitation anywhere in the reviewed materials. No file in the reviewed repository was modified by this review (integrity hash confirmed unchanged before and after).

## What was and wasn't assessed

**Assessed (this run):** Module 1 (transparency/documentation review) was performed against 20 auto-discovered and in-repo documentation sources (AGENTS.md, sibling `docs/README.md`, CLAUDE.md, LICENSE, the in-repo Lancet Oncology manuscript draft, 12 rendered Quarto report families, four technical-documentation reports, and source/roxygen comments), by two independent LLM reviewers (documentation-completeness and documentation-consistency). Module 3 (verification) was performed on a read-only scratch copy of the model: behavioural black-box testing (56 tests including a base-case run, trace/partition invariants, extreme-value tests, a PSA batch of 100 iterations, and 9 unit-style tests of core functions), white-box code inspection (12 findings, including root-causing the black-box failures), and a coding-standards/CHAOS review (14 findings). The confidential patient-level trial data (`data/tidy/METIMMOX.rds`, `data/sensitive/*.xlsx`) was present locally, so the model could be executed rather than only statically inspected.

**Not assessed:** Module 2 (AI-simulated face-validity council), Module 4 (cross-validation against a comparator model), and Module 5 (external validation against independent observed event data) were **not requested** for this run; every checklist item owned by those modules is marked **Deferred** below rather than scored. No comparator model or external validation dataset was supplied to this run, and none was auto-discovered as reviewable evidence in the repository beyond a single narrative sentence in the manuscript comparing predicted 5-year OS to a published registry figure (which Module 1 records but does not itself validate). "Fable_5" in this report's naming refers to the AI model that performed this ValidateHE run (Claude Fable 5), not to a model-validation grading scale.

**Transparency disclosure:** This module is an AI-assisted documentation-completeness and documentation/code-consistency review. It establishes whether documentation is complete, findable, and consistent with static code artifacts — it does **not** by itself establish clinical validity or correct implementation (see Module 3 for that).

**Face-validity disclosure:** Not requested for this run.

**Cross-validation disclosure:** Not requested for this run.

**External-validation disclosure:** Not requested for this run.

## Top findings in plain language

- **We checked whether the progression-free-survival (PFS) curve ever exceeds the overall-survival (OS) curve** (a health-economic model should never have "more time free of progression" than "time alive"). It should not, by definition. Instead, for the CRP-guided and TMB/BRAF-guided biomarker-positive subgroups — the two arms the entire economic evaluation exists to assess — PFS exceeds OS across roughly **49-51% of the 10-year modeled horizon**. Root cause: OS and PFS are fitted as two separate parametric survival models, each independently chosen by AIC (`04_parametric_survival_analysis.R`), with nothing constraining the extrapolated curves to preserve OS ≥ PFS (findings `BB-PSM-ORD-crp`, `BB-PSM-ORD-tmb_braf`, `WB-001`). This is the single most important finding in this review and is why Module 3 verdicts Fail.
- **We checked how the code handles that curve crossing.** It applies `pfs <- pmin(pfs, os)` and emits a bare `warning()` — a message easily lost in a batch run or a 5,000-iteration PSA — which silently forces the "progressed" health state to exactly zero occupancy for the entire crossing region rather than surfacing the magnitude of the correction (`WB-003`). Because post-progression utility and end-of-life/follow-up costs differ materially from progression-free values, this silently redistributes QALYs and costs for the biomarker-positive arms without any reported flag of how much of the horizon was affected.
- **We checked whether documentation matches the deployed code for the set of biomarker strategies evaluated.** The currently-rendered reports and `AGENTS.md` consistently describe two economic strategies (CRP, TMB/BRAF) with TLR excluded by design. `docs/README.md` and the in-repo Lancet Oncology manuscript draft, however, still describe a third TLR-guided strategy and a "Model A/B/C" multi-structure comparison that a June 2026 refactor removed from the code (`TR-CONS-001`, `TR-CONS-002`). The manuscript's Model A/C and TLR-strategy headline results are therefore **not reproducible from the current repository under any settings**.
- **We checked which utility values the default configuration actually produces.** `AGENTS.md`'s parameter table documents the default as IPD-derived utilities (u_np=0.9077, u_p=0.9005), but the code's actual default (`UTILITY_SOURCE <- 1`) uses CORRECT-trial values (u_np=0.73, u_p=0.59); the manuscript's reported utilities (0.91/0.90) match the *documented* default, not the *code's* default (`TR-CONS-003`). A fresh clone run with default settings will not reproduce the manuscript's headline QALYs/ICERs.
- **We checked whether swapping two strategies' clinical-effect inputs produces a clean swap of outputs** (a standard verification test). QALYs and life-years swapped exactly, confirming the survival-curve/prevalence logic is sound, but costs did not: the CRP and TMB/BRAF diagnostic-test costs are attached by matching a hard-coded biomarker **name string** in `calculate_outcomes.R`, not by data carried with the strategy (`BB-SW`, `WB-004`). Not a base-case defect today, but a latent coupling that would silently misattribute costs if strategies are ever renamed or reordered.
- **We checked reproducibility infrastructure.** No `renv.lock`, no `DESCRIPTION` file, and no in-repo `README.md` (present in git history but currently deleted from the working tree) exist anywhere in the reviewed copy; all 37 detected packages are loaded via `pacman::p_load()` with no pinned versions (`CS-005`). Combined with the confidential trial data being intentionally excluded from the public repository, full independent reproduction by an outside party is not currently possible even though the documented run order and code structure are otherwise clear.
- **We checked whether any documented, independent human expert review of the conceptual model, input data, or implemented code exists.** None was found (`TR-COMP-011`, `TR-COMP-013`, `TR-COMP-015` — AdViSHE A1/B1/C1); the manuscript's own "Contributors" section is a `[To be completed]` placeholder.
- **On the positive side**, a 100-iteration PSA batch completed cleanly (0 run errors, 0% fallback-to-base-case-curve rate), the base case is fully deterministic on re-run, cohort conservation and state-occupancy bounds held for every strategy and every cycle, and CDA-AMC PSA-consistency items 43-46 all passed — the model's plumbing (discounting, cohort accounting, PSA sampling machinery) is sound; the defect is specifically in how the OS/PFS curves are extrapolated and reconciled.

## 2.2 Method: how this review was performed

This run used 5 isolated review agents plus orchestrator-performed inspection: two independent Module-1 (transparency) documentation reviewers (Sonnet) — one scoring documentation *completeness*, one scoring documentation/code *consistency*; and three Module-3 (verification) subagents — black-box behavioural testing (Sonnet), coding-standards/CHAOS review (Sonnet), and white-box code inspection. The white-box subagent was dispatched but was interrupted by a session limit before it could write findings; the white-box results in this report were instead produced by the ValidateHE orchestrator (Claude Fable) performing the deep root-cause code inspection directly, cross-referencing the black-box subagent's failures against the source code line-by-line. This substitution is disclosed here transparently rather than silently backfilled. All review agents worked exclusively on a read-only scratch copy; no file in the original repository was read-write accessed or modified.

### Module 1: transparency

Two LLM reviewers independently read the documentation corpus listed in §2.1/Appendix, without access to each other's output, then their findings were reconciled by the orchestrator. The completeness reviewer scored whether each CDA-AMC/AdViSHE/CHAOS documentation-layer item is present and findable; the consistency reviewer specifically hunted for contradictions between documents and between documentation and static code (e.g., grepping `model_configs.R` against README claims, comparing git-blame timestamps against documented defaults). Both reviewers independently converged on the same core problem before being reconciled, which is treated as corroborating evidence rather than double-counting.

### Module 2: face validity

Not requested.

### Module 3: verification

Black-box testing ran the model's base case and 27 additional behavioural probes (equalized effectiveness, extreme utilities/costs/mortality, discount-rate extremes, horizon changes, arm-swap, doubling/halving of effect size, a 100-iteration PSA batch) plus 9 unit-style tests of `validate_model_params()`, `calculate_outcomes()`, and `extract_all_survival_probabilities()`, all executed against the actual R code on the scratch copy (not simulated). White-box inspection traced the root cause of every black-box failure back to specific file:line locations in `model_fun.R`, `calculate_outcomes.R`, and `04_parametric_survival_analysis.R`, and independently verified the discounting formula, partition-sums-to-1 identity, and forward/backward traceability of two representative parameters. Coding-standards review scored the CHAOS v0.9 rubrics (folder structure, style, documentation, modularity, reproducibility) plus TECH-VER Stage-5 programming/efficiency concerns (DRY violations, loop idioms, error-masking patterns, hidden global dependencies).

### Module 4: cross-validation

Not requested.

### Module 5: external validation

Not requested.

## 2.3 Transparency results

**Documents reviewed (20 source ids):** 4 auto-discovered sibling docs (`AGENTS.md`, `docs/README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `LICENSE`), the in-repo manuscript (Lancet Oncology v4 draft), 12 Quarto report families (plus their rendered PDFs, extracted to text via `pdftotext`), 4 technical-documentation reports (`bug_fix_impact`, `age_effect_analysis`, `all_parametric_survival_models`, `model_b_comparison`), the bibliography, and roxygen/source comments. No `--docs` argument was supplied; sibling documentation was auto-discovered from the parent case directory (`docs/` sits alongside `model/`). Absent from the corpus: `DESCRIPTION`, `renv.lock`, `NEWS`/`CHANGELOG`, an in-repo `README.md` (it lives only in the sibling `docs/` folder), and a `METIMMOX.rds` data dictionary.

**Consensus (both reviewers independently converged):** a June 2026 single-model/no-TLR refactor (parent-repo commit `ab7a079`, "refactor stage 7: finish single-model/no-TLR cleanup, fix renders, regen outputs") was propagated to `AGENTS.md` and the currently-rendered economic reports, but **not** to the sibling `docs/README.md` or the in-repo manuscript, leaving three mutually inconsistent vintages of the strategy set describing the model. Five candidate contradictions were independently **confirmed** with file:line and git-history evidence:

1. `docs/README.md` lists TLR as a third economic strategy versus `model_configs.R:28` `ALL_STRATEGIES <- c("control","crp","tmb_braf")` (`TR-CONS-001`).
2. `docs/README.md` and the manuscript describe a "Model A/B/C" multi-structure comparison that no longer exists in code — `multi_model_cea.R` (despite its name) contains only single-model helper functions per its own header comment; the manuscript's Model A/C and TLR-strategy headline results are structurally unreproducible from current code (`TR-CONS-002`, `TR-CONS-007`).
3. `AGENTS.md`'s documented `UTILITY_SOURCE` default (0, IPD-derived) contradicts the code's actual default (1, CORRECT trial) at `02_setup_and_global_variables.R:59`; the manuscript's reported utility values match the documented (not the actual code) default, blocking reproduction of headline QALYs/ICERs (`TR-CONS-003`).
4. Dependency lists are prose-only (no `DESCRIPTION`/`renv.lock`) and omit roughly 14 packages actually used in the repository, mostly DAG/statistics-only reports (`TR-CONS-004`).
5. `docs/README.md`'s render guidance ("render the whole report directory at once") directly contradicts `AGENTS.md`'s explicit warning that economic reports must be rendered individually with `--to pdf` because their GFM pass fails (`TR-CONS-005`).

**Completeness gaps** (AdViSHE Parts A-D): no documented independent human review of the conceptual model (A1, `TR-COMP-011`), the input data (B1, `TR-COMP-013`), or the implemented code (C1, `TR-COMP-015`) was found anywhere in the corpus — the manuscript's own Contributors section is a `[To be completed]` placeholder. No documentation of extreme-value/stress-testing (C2, `TR-COMP-016`) or of a predefined unit-test acceptance protocol (C4, `TR-COMP-018`) exists, though the underlying test scripts themselves do (`scripts/R/tests/`). No comparison of model outputs against other published decision models is reported (D2, `TR-COMP-020`); the manuscript self-describes as "the first" such evaluation, which is plausible but not stated explicitly as a scoping decision. Empirical validation (D4) is limited to a single narrative sentence comparing predicted 5-year OS to a published registry figure, with no quantified agreement statistic or dependent/independent classification (`TR-COMP-022`).

**Module 1 verdict rationale:** applying Module 1 verdict rule 3, the Model-A/B/C+TLR-scope contradiction and the `UTILITY_SOURCE` default contradiction are each (a) uncorrected within the documentation set and (b) block reproduction of decision-driving outputs, routing the module to **"Insufficiently transparent for review."** `AGENTS.md` and the currently-rendered reports do consistently and adequately document the deployed single-model design; the defect is that the sibling `docs/README.md` and the manuscript were not updated to match it.

## 2.5 Black-box results

**Base case (`BB-BASE`, pass):** cost: control=20,867.2, crp=55,025.8, tmb_braf=60,797.5 (EUR); QALY: control=1.41414, crp=1.38424, tmb_braf=1.35303; LY: control=2.17082, crp=2.03532, tmb_braf=2.03304.

Of 56 black-box tests, **43 passed** cleanly (base-case run; QALY cross-check against the model's own internal aggregation; LY≥QALY; undiscounted≥discounted; QALY/LY ratio within the utility range; cohort-conservation, non-negativity, and absorbing-monotonicity for every trace and strategy; individual PFS/OS curve bounds and monotonicity for every strategy; utilities-forced-to-1/0; costs-forced-to-0; mortality-forced-to-~1; equalized-effectiveness; discount-rate extremes; shorter horizon; halving of effect difference; determinism re-run; all 4 PSA consistency checks (43-46); and all 9 unit-style tests of `validate_model_params`/`calculate_outcomes`/`extract_all_survival_probabilities`). The 10 fails and 3 not-tested items were:

| ID | Test | Verdict | Severity | Key result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BB-PSM-ORD-control | OS >= PFS, no crossing | Fail | critical (field)/minor (magnitude) | PFS exceeds OS at 3/521 points, t=1-3wk only, max excess 0.0005 — near-t0 numerical noise |
| BB-PSM-ORD-crp | OS >= PFS, no crossing | Fail | critical | PFS exceeds OS at 251/521 points (48%); 49% of the entire horizon (t=267-520wk, max excess 0.0229) in the crp+ subgroup; progressed state forced to 0 there |
| BB-PSM-ORD-tmb_braf | OS >= PFS, no crossing | Fail | critical | PFS exceeds OS at 186/521 points (36%); 51% of the entire horizon (t=254-520wk, max excess 0.0145) in the tmb_braf+ subgroup |
| BB-PSM-WCHECK-crp | Weighted curve reproduces precomputed field | Fail | major | 0.02pp prevalence drift between full-data (n=74) and complete-case (n=68) cohorts |
| BB-PSM-WCHECK-tmb_braf | Weighted curve reproduces precomputed field | Fail | major | 0.81pp prevalence drift (larger due to more missingness) |
| BB-M0 | Mortality=0: LY equals horizon | Fail | minor | Undiscounted LY = 10.019y vs 10y expected (equal across arms) — 521-point grid sum with no half-cycle correction over-counts by ~1 cycle (~0.19%), ICER-neutral |
| BB-EQ2 | Equal effect+cost: costs align | Fail | minor | CRP arm +16.0 EUR residual — CRP test cost shares a field with routine blood-monitoring cost, cannot be independently zeroed |
| BB-SW | Arm swap: outputs swap | Fail | major | QALYs/LYs swap exactly; costs do not (±2,502 EUR = NGS-vs-blood test-cost delta) — test cost keyed to biomarker name string, not data |
| BB-AC | Raise one arm's acquisition cost | Fail | minor | Bumping the shared nivolumab cost field raises both crp and tmb_braf (intentional — same drug — but no per-strategy price hook exists) |
| BB-2X | Double effect difference: ~2x incremental QALY | Fail | minor | Ratio 1.478, outside 30% band — compounded by probability-scale clamp saturation and the PSM-ORD crossing |
| BB-D2Y | (1+r)^2 spot check | Not-tested | info | Per-cycle streams not synthesized in the harness; QALY/LY discounting already independently verified via BB-D0/D1 |
| BB-HCC | Half-cycle correction toggle | Not-tested | info | No dedicated HCC setter exists (grep confirms no HCC logic at all); functionally the same gap as BB-M0 |
| BB-PSA-FALLBACK | PSA fallback rate | Not-tested | info | 0/100 iterations fell back to base-case curves at n=100 — healthy, but not exercised at the documented full n=5000 |

# Appendix B — Function inventory & dependency map

Parsed 39 `.R` file(s) and 386 `{r}` chunk(s) from 51 Rmd/qmd file(s); found 207 user-defined function(s). Chunk-derived entries are tagged `file#chunk-label` with lines mapped to the original document. Code was parsed statically, never executed.

**Duplicate definitions** (same name defined more than once — last `source()` wins silently): `strategy_label`, `format_eur`, `format_icer`, `biomarker_label`, `restricted_mean`, `plot_dag`, `complete_data`, `fmt_num`, `fmt_p`, `fmt_hr`, `fmt_or`, `run_wilcox_test`, `run_fisher_test`, `run_mh_test`, `run_firth_cox_test`, `run_firth_logistic_test`, `run_permutation_test`, `edge_support_label`, `ci_support_label`, `predict_pop_avg`, `extract_km_data`, `fit_firth_cox`, `extract_coxphf_results`, `get_interaction_hr`, `extract_ridge_interaction`, `get_strategies`, `get_biomarkers`, `fmt_eur`, `fit_all_direct` (see `CS-007` for the risk this poses).

**Core call chain:** `get_current_model_config()` → `get_strategies()`/`get_biomarkers()`/`get_strategy_formula()` → `model_fun()` → `generate_psa_control_predictions()`/`generate_psa_population_averaged_predictions()` (PSA mode) or population-averaged prediction functions (deterministic mode) → `calculate_outcomes()`. `run_basecase()` (in `multi_model_cea.R`, despite its name — see `CS-011`/`TR-CONS-007`) orchestrates the deterministic base case; `run_psa_analysis()` orchestrates PSA; `run_evppi_analysis()`/`run_scenario_analysis()` sit downstream of the PSA cache.

**Key functions and locations** (selected): `model_fun` (`scripts/R/functions/model_fun.R:97`) — main PSM engine; `calculate_outcomes` (`scripts/R/functions/calculate_outcomes.R:2`) — cost/QALY aggregation, called by `model_fun` and `run_enriched_analysis`; `validate_model_params` (`model_fun.R:38`); `get_current_model_config`/`get_strategies`/`get_biomarkers`/`get_strategy_formula`/`get_control_formula` (`model_configs.R:44-136`) — single source of truth for the strategy/biomarker/formula set; `generate_population_averaged_predictions` / `generate_population_averaged_predictions_multimodel` (`prediction_functions.R:39,208`); `run_basecase`/`load_psa_cache`/`create_ceac_plot`/`create_psa_summary_table` (`multi_model_cea.R:33-235`); `run_psa_analysis`/`generate_psa_samples` (`psa_functions.R:8,47`); `run_evppi_analysis`/`calculate_evppi_improved`/`calculate_population_evppi` (`evppi_functions.R:12,187,329`); `run_scenario_psa`/`run_scenario_evppi`/`run_all_scenarios` (`scenario_analysis.R:51,122,216`); `get_git_commit`/`collect_metadata`/`select_snapshots_for_comparison` (`snapshot_utils.R`) — snapshot/bug-fix-impact tooling.
